config.title: Inline Styles

intro.title: Inline Styles
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React component that uses inline styles to change the appearance of text and a button. You will learn how to apply styles directly within JSX using JavaScript objects, which is a core React concept for dynamic styling. The main technologies involved are React, TypeScript, and JSX, focusing on style objects with camelCase property names. This approach is beginner-friendly and allows you to see immediate visual feedback as you code.
intro.usecase: Inline styles in React are commonly used for dynamic, state-driven UI elements where styles need to change instantly based on user interaction or data. You'll see this pattern in interactive dashboards where metric cards change color based on thresholds, form validation that shows real-time error highlighting, and draggable UI components where position updates continuously. Developers frequently use inline styles for quick prototyping, conditional styling in components like toggle switches or progress bars, and when integrating with animation libraries that require direct style manipulation.

objectives: Apply inline styles directly to JSX elements using the style attribute.
Construct a TypeScript object to define CSS properties and values for inline styling.
Manipulate style objects dynamically by updating their properties based on component state.
Integrate inline styles with event handlers to create interactive visual feedback.
Configure conditional styling by applying different style objects based on logical conditions.
Initialize and bind style objects to multiple elements to maintain consistent styling across a component.
Render components with inline styles that adapt to user interactions and state changes.

steps.title: Import React
steps.instruction: Import React from the 'react' library to use JSX and create components.
steps.hint: Add the import statement at the top of your file. This gives you access to React's functionality.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing a library
import React from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The React library is imported, enabling you to write JSX and create React components.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing React specifically from the 'react' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: import React from the 'react' library to use JSX and React features.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns a JSX element. Use either the React.FC type or an explicit return type annotation.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function named App that returns some JSX content.
steps.seedCode:
// Import React here

// Create the App component here
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined and ready to return JSX content.
successCriteria: A functional component named App is created with proper TypeScript typing.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've defined a component named App that returns JSX content.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component isn't defined correctly. Check that you've created a function named App that returns JSX.

steps.title: Add a div element with basic inline style
steps.instruction: Inside your App component's return statement, add a div element with a style attribute. Set the style to an object with backgroundColor: 'lightblue'.
steps.hint: In JSX, the style attribute accepts a JavaScript object where CSS properties are written in camelCase.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component now returns a div element with a light blue background color applied via inline styles.
successCriteria: The App component returns a div element with a style attribute containing an object that sets backgroundColor to 'lightblue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the style attribute with a JavaScript object (double curly braces) and setting backgroundColor to 'lightblue'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires adding a div element with inline styles. Check that you're using the style attribute correctly with a JavaScript object containing backgroundColor: 'lightblue'.

steps.title: Add text content to the styled div
steps.instruction: Inside the div element that has the inline style, add the text content 'Hello, styled div!'.
steps.hint: You can place text directly between the opening and closing div tags.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding text inside an element
This text will appear in red.
steps.expectedOutcome: The div with the light blue background will now display the text 'Hello, styled div!'.
successCriteria: The text 'Hello, styled div!' appears inside the div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some content, but make sure it's exactly 'Hello, styled div!' inside the div.
steps.feedbackWrong: The text content wasn't added correctly. Place 'Hello, styled div!' directly between the opening and closing div tags.

steps.title: Add a second style property to the div
steps.instruction: In the style object of your existing div, add a second property to set padding to '20px'.
steps.hint: Add a comma after the existing backgroundColor property, then add a new property like padding: '20px'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The div element will have both a light blue background and 20px padding applied through inline styles.
successCriteria: The style object includes both backgroundColor and padding properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added the padding property correctly within the style object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The style object should include both backgroundColor and padding properties. Check your syntax and try again.

steps.title: Define a style object variable
steps.instruction: Before the return statement in your App component, declare a variable named 'boxStyle' using const, assign it an object with border and margin properties, and type it as React.CSSProperties.
steps.hint: Define the variable above the return statement. Use the syntax: const boxStyle: React.CSSProperties = { border: '...', margin: '...' }.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a typed style object variable defined inside the component, ready to be used in JSX.
successCriteria: A variable named 'boxStyle' is declared with const, typed as React.CSSProperties, and contains border and margin properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You defined a style object, but check: is it typed as React.CSSProperties? Does it have both border and margin properties?
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires declaring a typed style object variable before the return statement. Try: const boxStyle: React.CSSProperties = { border: '2px solid black', margin: '20px' };

steps.title: Apply the style object variable to a new element
steps.instruction: Add a new div element inside your component's return statement. Set its style attribute to reference the boxStyle variable you defined earlier (e.g., style={boxStyle}).
steps.hint: Place the new div element after the existing styled div. Use the style attribute with curly braces to reference the variable.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component will now have two div elements: one with inline style object and another using the boxStyle variable.
successCriteria: A new div element is added
The new div's style attribute references boxStyle variable
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a new element, but make sure its style attribute references the boxStyle variable using curly braces (style={boxStyle}).
steps.feedbackWrong: The new div element should reference the boxStyle variable in its style attribute. Check that you're using the correct variable name and syntax.

steps.title: Combine inline and variable-based styles
steps.instruction: In your component, modify the existing div element to combine the boxStyle variable with additional inline styles using the spread operator.
steps.hint: Use the spread operator (...) to merge the boxStyle object with new style properties directly in the style attribute.
steps.expectedOutcome: The div element should have its style attribute updated to combine the boxStyle variable with at least one additional inline property using the spread operator.
successCriteria: The div's style attribute uses the spread operator (...)
boxStyle is merged with additional inline properties
The code compiles without TypeScript errors
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using the spread operator (...) to merge the boxStyle object with additional properties in the style attribute.
steps.feedbackWrong: The spread operator wasn't used correctly to combine the style objects. Review how to merge objects using ... in the style attribute.

steps.title: Export the App component
steps.instruction: Export the App component as the default export from the file.
steps.hint: Use the export default syntax to make the App component available for import in other files.
steps.analogousExample:
// Export a component as default
export default App;
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is exported as the default export, making it ready to be imported and used in other parts of the application.
successCriteria: App component is exported as default
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using the correct export syntax: 'export default App;'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component needs to be exported as the default export. Add 'export default App;' at the end of the file.
